promotion_note: Promoted 2026-07-25 (miso-88): the 2026-07-24-miso-86-netrev-margin keeper form replayed byte-faithfully (gas_offer_margin=true, carry_operating_mothballs=true, outages on the CAMPD unit-level derate) with a SINGLE delta that is a DATA CORRECTION, not a mechanism or a flag: the eGRID plant-heat-rate boundary reconciliation. eGRID keys PLNT23 on ORISPL, but CEMS reports co-located plants sharing a stack under one facilityId, so where that happens the plant row's heat input PLHTIAN spans the whole CEMS facility while its net generation PLNGENAN covers only the one EIA plant. Riverside Energy Center (55641, MISO-East) is the live instance: PLHTIAN 53,017,211 MMBtu is byte-identical to the CAMPD heatInput sum over all four units of facility 55641 -- the 2004 Riverside block AND the 2020 West Riverside block (EIA 64020, 454 m away) -- while PLNGENAN 3,543,044 MWh is the 674.9 MW Riverside plant alone; eGRID's own UNT23 sheet dates the two surplus units to 2019 against EIA-860 vintages of 2004, and 64020 reports the same machines independently. The published 14.964 MMBtu/MWh is ~2x any combined cycle and priced the plant near $45/MWh against ~$20/MWh for its class -- above most MISO coal -- so the LP never committed it (model CF 0.01/0.05/0.01 vs actual 0.60/0.57/0.56). Reconciled to 6.880 from eGRID's own unit rows, cross-validated three independent ways. ZERO degrees of freedom; rule 11's named boundary-mismatch exception, reconciled rather than guessed. Accepted under four conditions, the last self-validating, which is what rejects the two would-be false positives (Devon 544, King City 10294); across all six ISOs the accepted set is exactly {55641: 6.880} and the verified blast radius is 3 rows / 1 plant / MISO only. A general form was sized and REFUSED (47 plants touched, 25 destroyed). RESULT: closes the keeper's sole load-bearing VOLUME fail -- C1 fuel-mix FAIL -> PASS, with CC_REGULAR improving in all three years (2023 -6.71 -> -4.99 TWh, 2024 -2.09 -> -0.42, 2025 -6.14 -> -4.19). Determination stays NOT-YET but on ONE fail instead of two: C3b-2025 price shape (NRMSE 0.204 -> 0.208, veto <=0.20). Both worsened price crossings (C3b, and the ledgered C3a-2025 caveat widening -14.8% -> -16.6%) were PRE-REGISTERED in the charter before solving as the arithmetic consequence of returning 534.8 MW of cheap CC to the merit order, and are KEPT per rules 1/11 -- the accurate input stays in even though it worsens the fit, and the worse fit is a discovered-bug signal to root-cause in the 2025 summer-body price lane (FINDING-miso87-c3b-summer-2025-body-2026-07.md), never to be offset with a tuned adder. Promoted on STRUCTURAL FIDELITY (rule 1: the keeper is the most faithful run, not the lowest MAE), since the superseded keeper carries a provably wrong measured heat rate. Rule 22 LOO: the correction has zero DOF and one value identical in every year, so nothing is year-specific to overfit, and the C1 gain is uniform across 2023/2024/2025. Full span in ONE bundle (rule 16). Charter: docs/handoffs/miso-88-egrid-hr-boundary-plan-2026-07.md. Supersedes 2026-07-24-miso-86-netrev-margin (same recipe + this input correction). RE-GATED 2026-07-26 (miso-90, OWNER DECISION): determination NOT-YET -> CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS. No re-solve, no bundle regeneration, no config change -- the sole delta is that C3b-2025 is now LEDGERED as an instrument-blocked measurement gap, on the same template as the C3c tail. miso-89 established the finding the entry rests on (results/calibration/FINDING-miso89-diurnal-spread-compression-2026-07.md): the C3b miss is NOT a 2025 level error but standing diurnal-spread compression (the model reproduces only 29-47% of the observed peak-minus-night spread in every season of every year, and 2025 breaches the veto only because the ACTUAL summer spread widened 26.3 -> 32.7 $/MWh while the model's stayed flat 11.7 -> 12.2); its driver is a ~10 GW under-derate of 2025 summer-peak fossil availability, established by difference-in-differences so that no cross-fuel attribution is required (model fossil derate at Jun/Jul HE16-18 is flat at +1.76 GW into 2025 while MISO's published offline record jumps +12.32 GW, breaking a ~14.6 GW stable offset to 24.76 GW); and every enumerated instrument for it is refuted (miso-85 uniform attribution, miso-87 cross-fuel attribution), adjudicated data-blocked (miso-78/79 congestion), or measured INERT (gt_ambient_derate removes 0 MW -- zone-mean TMAX clears its 35 C reference in 0 h at summer peak in any year). It cannot be closed by adding a pricing mechanism: MISO's scarcity apparatus is already built and live in this keeper and prices in 0/6/2 hours of 8760 -- STARVED, not missing -- and nothing availability-sized can arm it, since the model already carries 31.9 GW of idle fossil headroom at summer peak against a 2.64 GW reserve requirement (>12x slack). Ledgered per rule 24: no measured source resolves at the needed grain, so the honest outcome is to document, size and stop rather than tune. The entry explicitly does NOT license an offer adder, a summer multiplier, or widening the C3c ledger to absorb it. A standing DATA ASK is opened alongside it for MISO outage data at UNIT or FUEL grain (docs/handoffs/miso-outage-grain-data-ask-2026-07.md), which is the only thing that would reopen the lane honestly. GOVERNANCE NOTE: this saturates the non-protective ledgered-caveat budget at 3/3 (C3a, C3b, C3c) -- no further load-bearing criterion can be ledgered for MISO without exceeding it, so the next load-bearing miss must be BUILT, not documented.
